help_camera_body:
Camera scanning is a Premium feature, available with an active subscription.

Tap the camera button (bottom-right) to open the live preview. Frame your blood pressure monitor's display inside the on-screen guide, then tap Capture.

The photo is sent to Gemini 2.5 Flash, which reads the Systolic, Diastolic, and Pulse values. You can review and correct them on the next screen before saving.

If you don't have an active subscription, tapping the camera button will open the upgrade screen where you can subscribe or restore a previous purchase.
help_export_body:
Tap the Share icon in the top bar to export your data. A dropdown offers three formats:

• JSON — your complete reading history. Can be imported back into the app.
• CSV — your complete history in spreadsheet format, compatible with Excel or Google Sheets.
• PDF — a multi-page document containing:
  – Landscape trend charts for the last 7, 30, and 90 days. Each chart includes reference lines and a stats bar (avg / min / max). Tagged readings are marked with numbered badges, and a legend below the chart maps each number to its tag — a reading with several tags shows their numbers combined (e.g. 247).
  – A portrait table of readings from the last 30 days with colour-coded categories and their tags.

The PDF charts follow the Avg setting from the Dashboard. With Avg on, back-to-back readings are merged into one point on the charts, while the readings table always lists every individual entry.

The export is shared via Android's standard share sheet.
help_hc_body:
Health Connect is Google's on-device health data platform. This app can write your readings as Blood Pressure and Heart Rate records.

Bulk sync: tap the heart-monitor icon in the top bar. You will be asked to grant write permissions the first time. All existing readings are uploaded (safe to repeat — existing records are updated, not duplicated).

If Health Connect is not installed on your device, the app will offer a link to the Play Store to install it.
help_hemo_body:
Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) is the average pressure in your arteries across a full heartbeat — roughly diastolic plus one-third of the gap to systolic. A normal resting MAP is typically 70–100 mmHg.

Pulse Pressure (PP) is simply systolic minus diastolic. A value between 40–60 mmHg is typical at rest. A persistently high pulse pressure (above ~60 mmHg) can be a sign of arterial stiffness.

Both values are derived from your saved systolic and diastolic readings. They are shown for information only — please discuss them with your healthcare professional.
help_history_body:
All readings are listed below the chart, newest first. Each row shows:

• Date and time
• SYS / DIA · pulse (bpm)
• A colour-coded zone badge
• Context tag chips (if any have been set)
• Any note you added (shown in italics)

Swipe a row left or right to delete it. A snackbar appears at the bottom with an Undo button — you have 5 seconds to reverse the deletion before it is permanent.

Long-press any row to open the tag editor. Select or deselect the context tags (Caffeine, Alcohol, Salty meal, Exercise, Stress, Poor sleep, Resting, On waking), then tap Save. Tags let you correlate lifestyle factors with your readings and power the Insights card.
help_import_body:
Tap the Download icon (top bar) to import readings from a JSON file previously exported from this app.

The app opens a file picker. Select your JSON export file. Only readings whose timestamps do not already exist in the database are inserted — re-importing the same file is safe.

A snackbar confirms how many new readings were added, or tells you there was nothing new to import.
help_insights_body:
When you have enough readings, an Insights card appears on the dashboard above the reading list. It surfaces patterns detected entirely on your device — no data ever leaves your phone.

Pattern types:

• Morning vs evening — whether your morning or evening readings consistently run higher
• 30-day trend — whether your systolic is drifting up or down over the last month
• Time in range — the share of recent readings that fell in a healthy range
• Healthy streak — how many readings in a row landed in a healthy range
• Weekday vs weekend — whether there is a consistent gap between work days and rest days
• Tag correlation — which context tag is most strongly linked to higher or lower readings

Each insight is colour-coded: green means positive, amber means something to watch, grey is neutral. Tap "N more" to expand all detected insights; tap "Show less" to collapse.

Insights require a minimum number of readings before they appear — a few days of data is usually enough to start seeing your first patterns.
help_manual_body:
Tap the pencil button to enter a reading without taking a photo. The sliders are pre-filled with your last saved reading (defaults: 120 / 80 / 60 on first launch).

Adjust Systolic, Diastolic, and Pulse using the slider or the ± buttons. Add an optional note, then tap Save Reading.

The Save button is disabled until Systolic is greater than Diastolic.
help_profile_body:
Tap the Person icon to open your profile. Filling it in helps personalise the app.

Fields available:

• Birth year
• Biological sex
• Weight (kg) and Height (cm) — live BMI preview shown
• Physical activity level

All data stays on your device. The profile is optional; the app works fully without it.
help_reminders_body:
Tap the Bell icon to configure daily measurement reminders.

1. Grant the notification permission if prompted.
2. Enable the master switch.
3. Set a Morning time (ideally 30 minutes after waking, before coffee or medication).
4. Set an Evening time (when you are relaxed and at rest).

Notifications include a Log Now shortcut that opens the app, and a Snooze (15m) action. Alarms are re-scheduled automatically each day and survive device reboots.

If the exact-alarm permission is not available on your device, the app will direct you to the system settings to enable it.
help_risk_body:
When at least one reading exists, a Health Risk card appears at the top of the reading list. It combines your latest BP category with your health profile to surface contextual guidance.

Guidance is drawn from AHA (American Heart Association) guidelines and is prefixed with a disclaimer. It is informational only and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional.

Tap "Edit profile" on the card to complete or update your health profile.
help_trends_body:
The chart on the Dashboard plots Systolic and Diastolic readings over time. Use the chips above the chart to filter the view:

• 7d — last 7 days
• 30d — last 30 days (default)
• 90d — last 90 days
• All — complete history

The Y-axis adapts to your data. With fewer than 24 hours of readings it is fixed at 40–180 mmHg. Once your history spans 24 hours or more, the axis tightens around your actual range (±5 mmHg padding, snapped to the nearest 10) so trends are easier to see.

The Avg chip, to the right of the range chips, smooths bursts of readings: when it is on, measurements taken within about 10 minutes of each other are averaged into a single point — the standard way to read repeated readings. Turn it off to plot every individual reading. This affects only the chart; your reading list always keeps every entry.

Rotate the phone to landscape for a full-screen chart view.

The Trend / Scatter switch below the filters changes how readings are drawn. Trend shows them over time; Scatter is a 3D plot — diastolic and systolic on the front face and pulse as depth. Drag with one finger to rotate it and reveal the pulse axis; tap Scatter again to snap back to the front view. The range filters apply to both views, and your choice is remembered the next time you open the app.
